discovery: Discovery of geometric and topological phases in quantum mechanics (the Aharonov-Bohm effect and the Berry phase)

nominees.name: Yakir Aharonov
nominees.affiliation: Tel Aviv University, Israel and Chapman University, USA

subfield: Quantum foundations / quantum and topological physics
motivation: Aharonov (with the late David Bohm, 1959) showed that electromagnetic potentials, long dismissed as mathematical conveniences, produce observable phase shifts for charged particles moving only through field-free regions. Berry (1984) showed that any quantum system carried adiabatically around a closed loop in parameter space acquires a geometric phase that depends only on the loop's geometry. Together these insights showed that quantum states carry nonlocal, geometric information that classical intuition forbids. Both effects have been confirmed many times, from electron holography and mesoscopic rings to polarization optics and cold atoms. The geometric phase is now central to modern physics: it underlies the Berry curvature of electronic bands, the anomalous and quantum Hall effects, topological insulators, the modern theory of polarization, and geometric quantum gates. Few theoretical ideas have so thoroughly changed how physicists think about quantum mechanics while also opening such broad experimental territory.
